No option can be put forward yet, because the model could not assess your churn constraint.

- The limit is recorded as **monthly churn < 4%**, but churn is modelled as an outcome rather than measured on the constraint’s scale, so none of the options was tested for compliance with it.
- The comparison is only moderately robust and partly rests on a machine default of **£0 non‑Pro MRR**, not user evidence. Active Pro subscribers are the largest structural driver; their source is not recorded.
- The £20k MRR threshold also could not be scored against outcomes because the model lacks a starting MRR baseline and an explicit target frame.

So this run compares modelled MRR effects, but does not answer whether a price rise meets both parts of your stated goal.
